description: Ignitis is passionate about space, science, and exploration. Through our project, "Echoes of Exploration," we aim to uncover the stories and scientific significance of human-made objects left on the Moon and Mars through research and creative visual storytelling.
summary:
Echoes of Exploration is a digital educational storytelling exhibit about selected human-made equipment left on the Moon and Mars during space exploration missions.

The project introduces school-age learners to the stories behind these machines, explaining why they were sent, what they were designed to do, how their missions progressed, and what scientific knowledge they helped make possible.

Through a collection of illustrated mission stories, timelines, photographs, and simple scientific explanations, visitors can explore the history and legacy of robotic and human-assisted exploration beyond Earth.

The project highlights an important idea: even when a spacecraft or rover stops operating, the scientific knowledge gained from its mission continues to contribute to future exploration.

Our goal is to make planetary exploration easier to understand, visually engaging, and inspiring for young learners.
details: ECHOES OF EXPLORATION The machines we left behind. The discoveries that remain. 1. Introduction Space exploration has sent many spacecraft, landers, rovers and scientific instruments beyond Earth. Some of these machines completed their missions and remained on the Moon or Mars, while others stopped communicating or continued travelling through space. Although their operational missions ended, their contributions to science remain valuable. Echoes of Exploration is a digital educational storytelling exhibit that presents the history and scientific importance of selected equipment left on the Moon and Mars. 2. Project Objectives The main objectives are: - To introduce school-age learners to human-made equipment left on the Moon and Mars. - To explain the purpose and functions of selected spacecraft, landers and rovers. - To present important mission events and timelines. - To explain the scientific discoveries and engineering achievements associated with these missions. - To encourage curiosity about planetary science, robotics and space exploration. 3. Equipment Featured in the Project The exhibit focuses on four examples. A. Surveyor 3 — Moon (1967) Surveyor 3 was a robotic lunar lander launched by NASA in April 1967. It landed on the Moon on April 20, 1967. It carried a television camera and a surface-sampling instrument to investigate lunar soil. Its observations helped scientists understand the strength and characteristics of the lunar surface. In November 1969, Apollo 12 astronauts visited the lander and recovered selected components, including its camera system and soil scoop, for examination on Earth. Scientific importance: Surveyor 3 helped demonstrate that the lunar surface could support an Apollo lunar module and provided valuable information about the lunar environment. B. Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle — Moon (1971) Apollo 15 was the first Apollo mission to use the Lunar Roving Vehicle. This battery-powered electric vehicle allowed astronauts to travel farther across the lunar surface, carry scientific equipment and collect geological samples. The rover greatly increased the range and productivity of lunar surface exploration. It remained on the Moon after the astronauts departed. Scientific importance: The Lunar Roving Vehicle expanded human mobility and enabled more extensive geological investigations. C. Sojourner — Mars Pathfinder (1997) Sojourner was a small robotic rover deployed by the Mars Pathfinder mission in July 1997. It was the first wheeled vehicle to operate on another planet. It examined nearby rocks and soil, collected images and made scientific measurements. Although its planned mission was seven days, it operated for 83 days. Scientific importance: Sojourner demonstrated the usefulness of robotic mobility on Mars and helped establish technologies and methods used by later Mars rover missions. D. Opportunity — Mars (2004–2018) Opportunity was one of NASA's Mars Exploration Rovers. It investigated Martian rocks and soil to study evidence of past water activity. The rover was originally designed for a 90-Martian-day mission but operated for almost 15 years and travelled approximately 45.16 kilometres. A major dust storm in 2018 reduced the sunlight reaching its solar panels. The rover stopped communicating in June 2018, and NASA declared the mission complete in February 2019. Scientific importance: Opportunity provided extensive evidence about the history of water on Mars and greatly expanded our understanding of the planet's geological history. 4. How the Exhibit Works The project is organised into two main sections: Moon Exploration and Mars Exploration. Each equipment story includes: - Equipment name and mission year. - Destination and mission background. - Original purpose and functions. - Important mission events. - Mission status and final location, where supported by NASA sources. - Scientific contributions and discoveries. - Relevant photographs and explanatory illustrations. Visitors can follow the mission stories in a simple sequence and understand how each piece of equipment contributed to space exploration. 5. Target Audience The main target audience includes school-age students, teachers, young space enthusiasts and beginners interested in astronomy and planetary exploration. The project uses simple language and visual storytelling to make technical mission information accessible to a wider audience. 6. Expected Benefits The exhibit makes space exploration history easier to understand and encourages interest in science, engineering and robotics. It also demonstrates how robotic missions can contribute to scientific knowledge even after their operational lifetimes have ended. 7. Tools and Development Method The project is prepared as a digital educational exhibit and presentation using document and presentation-design tools. NASA's publicly available mission information, mission photographs and scientific resources are used for research and factual references. ChatGPT was used to assist with organising the project structure, drafting and simplifying explanations, and preparing presentation content. The team must review and verify the material before submission. No custom software application, interactive website or original robotic hardware is claimed as part of this project. 8. Conclusion Echoes of Exploration presents the stories of machines that helped humanity explore the Moon and Mars. Their missions demonstrate the importance of scientific curiosity, engineering innovation and robotic exploration. Although some of these machines no longer operate, their discoveries continue to influence our understanding of other worlds and inspire future missions.
